q-54452.name: Question 1
q-54452.worked_solution:
Let's sketch the graph of $y=\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x-1).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14274353/assets/c7c31f916c716ce9e6f881e8086d225d47ebe1b1e80e112a35a590fb7ad64840.png)

The function is not defined for $x\le \frac{1}{2}.$ Therefore,

$$
{lim}_{x\to 1/{2}^{-}}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x-1)=\text{DNE}.
$$

However, the function is defined for $x>\frac{1}{2}.$ Moreover,

$$
{lim}_{x\to 1/{2}^{+}}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x-1)=-\infty .
$$

Since the left and right-sided limits are not equal, we have

$$
{lim}_{x\to 1/2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x-1)=\text{DNE}.
$$
